description: The chart displays two pie charts side by side, each representing the error analysis for a different model: the Vanilla model on the left and the HCL model on the right, as indicated by the caption. Both charts are segmented into four categories, as defined by the legend at the top: “Atomic Skill Fail” (dark teal), “Correct” (medium teal), “Reason Error” (light teal), and “Question Misunderstood” (white). The left pie chart, for the Vanilla model, shows “Atomic Skill Fail” as the largest segment at 68.0%, followed by “Correct” at 12.0%, “Reason Error” at 12.0%, and “Question Misunderstood” at 8.0%. The right pie chart, for the HCL model, shows “Question Misunderstood” as the largest segment at 55.0%, followed by “Correct” at 21.0%, “Reason Error” at 14.0%, and “Atomic Skill Fail” at 10.0%. Each slice is labeled with its corresponding percentage value and color-coded to match the legend, with no slices exploded or visually emphasized beyond their proportional size. The segments in each chart appear to be arranged in descending order of percentage.
